[Rating: 1/10] This is a game that has simple rules, simple strategy and absolutely no depth. Played twice and it was completely lost on me why its popular. Then it made sense - it’s pretty!   Gameplay > Aestetics people! Prettier (usually) means shittier, especially in the case of Seikatsu.

I actually own Seikatsu: A Pet's Life, which is basically a retheme of Seikatsu with pets instead of birds. I thought perhaps having dogs on it would make it more fun for me (I LOVE dogs), but after playing the original Seikatsu—not even the version I own—I REALLY disliked the game. [Rating: 3/10] A unique victory points game that is slightly sullied by its odd 2-3 player set up that can make lining up pieces confusing with 2 players. Plays best with 3 players. I have other victory point games that are more fun. Sold it and wouldnt really care to play again.

[Rating: 3/10] This seems like a good example of a game that's more interesting for the designer than the players. Players each read the board in a different direction for scoring-- how interesting! Except for any given player, it doesn't matter. We could just as well be playing with the same scoring rubric except that my opponents are bad at the game and doing things which don't benefit them much. As far as I can tell, maximizing your score on each individual turn is all you need to do.  Maybe I missed something? The BGG ratings are surprisingly high for just HOW basic this appeared to be. [Rating: 3/10] A simple and beautiful looking abstract game with a Japanese theme. + Quick to play ± The concept of rows scoring in different directions for different players is neat, in practice it was harder to see its effect – Graphics made it hard to distinguish between some flowers – Needs more tension for this to have a higher rating

[Rating: 3/10] Neat little game. This is the kind of abstract Knizia would come up with. Hints of Ingenious and Kingdoms. I thought I'd like it more at 3 players, however I was surprised to find it too chaotic. Ah well

[Rating: 4/10] To be fair it was taught totally wrong the first play and it was terrible. Knowing that we played again and it worked better. at the end of the day it didn't do anything for me and I didn't feel like I was making any fun choices. At least it is fast, but not a game I would return to.

[Rating: 4/10] In the genre of "pleasant, pretty, undemanding games by Westerners on Japanese themes" this is better than Tokaido or Takenoko but not as good as Hanabi. It's also faster, smaller and less fussy than Kingdom Builder or Carcassonne in the genre of "make the obvious move, draw a tile, repeat".  Alas, more or less relegated to irrelevance by the advent of Azul which is an approachable abstract game with pretty tiles that is more interactive and interesting.
